# Glossary

Bob's shared vocabulary, generated from the glossary memory web.

### Album Note {#album-note}

A root-level Bob vault Markdown note with frontmatter `type: "[[album]]"` that owns
one record-note schema and its record folder. The note stem is the folder name and the
capture route. Its `parent` names an area or project, and its `summary` describes the
collection. The nested `record:` mapping defines the record noun, label, date policy,
and ordered fields. `bob albums sync` maintains the generated index and the owner's
machine-owned `## Albums` catalog. Albums are not notebooks, task types, task homes, or
root parents: parent and type walks pass through them to the area or project above.
Record notes are created and updated with `bob records new|update` or capture. See
`docs/records.md`.

### Annotation Section {#annotation-section}

*Aliases: section tag, section card.*

A named group of Highlights annotations inside a [Reference Note](#reference-note)'s managed
`## Highlights` region. A `# Name` line declares it: the first line of a sticky note
(its later lines become the section's description) or of a highlight, underline, or
image comment (that annotation joins the section). Trailing `@alias` or `#alias`
tokens add match keys. An annotation joins by carrying `@name` or `#name` as a whole
token at the start or end of a line. Matching ignores case and punctuation, and a
matched tag is consumed, so a tag that still shows did not group. Mid-sentence tokens,
`#task` lines, and `\` escapes never join. The space matters: `# Memory` declares,
`#memory` joins. Each displayed block has one home, and a comment declaration beats
tags. Each section renders as `### Name`, then a `[!summary|section]` card captioned
`@tag · N highlights · Pages`, its `^s-<slug>` block, and its members under `####`
page captions, ahead of Other highlights and Removed highlights. `bob ref show` and
the Mac Refs panel group the same way. Membership is re-derived from the sidecar on
every scan and nothing new is stored. Tag edits never change `^h-` IDs, and a PDF with
no declaration renders unchanged. Not a Markdown `##` heading or a `bob capture`
[Task Drawer](#task-drawer). See `docs/highlights-ref-sync.md`.

### Area Note {#area-note}

A Bob vault Markdown file with frontmatter `type: "[[area]]"` for an ongoing sphere of
responsibility with no end state, such as `cash`, `job`, or `dev`. Unlike a
[Project Note](#project-note), it has no `^prj` task and no done/canceled lifecycle, so Bob always
treats it as open. Its `parent` names the area it sits under (`"[[area]]"` for a
top-level area); sub-areas and projects point `parent` at the area (or, for a
sub-project, the project) they belong to. Every `#task` belongs in exactly one area or
project note by residence, the file holding its checkbox line; a [Task Link](#task-link) or embed
elsewhere never moves it. Area notes hold the ongoing tasks, usually under `## Tasks`,
that belong to no finite project; the inboxes (`inbox`, `mac_inbox`, `gkeep_inbox`) are
area notes whose tasks await triage. The only exceptions are each daily note's templated `^gtd` task, [Event Task](#event-task) rows under `## Events`, and closed tasks that `bob task archive` moved into `done/`; move any other stray task with Ctrl+Shift+M.
Root-level area notes are `@route` capture targets, and every area note gets the
per-note Ready cap and `## Tasks` status grouping. `offclock: true|false` sets the clock default for tasks on the root walk beneath it; `offclock_types` sets the clock off only for tasks whose effective type is listed. When both keys are present, `offclock_types` decides (see [Off-Clock Note Defaults Filter By Task Type](../develop/decisions.md#off-clock-note-defaults-filter-by-task-type) and [Off-Clock Follows Tag Then Note Default](../develop/decisions.md#off-clock-follows-tag-then-note-default)).
Each area or project also lists its descendant albums in a machine-owned `## Albums`
catalog maintained by `bob albums sync`, beside the `## Notebooks` catalog.

### Bank Month Note {#bank-month-note}

*Aliases: bank month, month note.*

A Bob vault note at `bank/YYYY-MM.md` under the bank hub (`bank.md`), with
`type: "[[bank_month]]"`, `parent: "[[bank]]"`, and `month: YYYY-MM`. The
filename is authoritative. It reads like a statement: one `##` heading per
day, oldest first, and [Bank Row](#bank-row)s beneath. Bob writes the note once from
the canonical template (`bob bank ensure` or `bob bank import`). Totals on
the month card and in `bob bank report` are drawn at read time and never
written into the note. Not a [Notebook](#notebook), an album, or a
[Period Note](#period-note). See `docs/bank.md`.

### Bank Row {#bank-row}

*Aliases: bank row, transaction row.*

One posted transaction or deposit as a top-level checkbox line under a day
heading in a [Bank Month Note](#bank-month-note) (`- [x] $13.71 Smashburger [cat:: dining]`).
`[ ]` means waiting and `[x]` means acknowledged. Typed rows start ticked;
`bob bank import` writes the rest unchecked, once. Bob later only ticks a
waiting row (`ack`) or appends `^bank-<hex>` to a typed row it matched.
Ctrl+Enter on a waiting row opens the Category card, which ticks it and files
`[cat:: key]` in one gesture, then lands on the next waiting row. It
never carries `#task`, so it is never a task, and it is never a record
note. `bob bank check` lints every row. See `docs/bank.md`.

### Bulk Capture {#bulk-capture}

*Aliases: multi-item capture, batch capture.*

A bulk capture holds multiple items: blank-line items, bare-URL lists, chained session operators, or one item per row from a `%t` template draft. Template rows are later nonblank physical lines, one capture per line (a template using only `{0}` takes one capture per space-separated or quoted value, so several can share a line), never blank-line-separated items; capturing the draft is exactly capturing its `bob capture -E` expansion. Blank or whitespace-only lines separate items; a blank-line-free block of two or more
bare-URL lines splits into one item per URL, and a line chaining session operators
(`+2 x`, `x =`) into one item per operator. A lone `@file` or `@file#section`
header line followed by bullets is a list instead: each first-level bullet
(with its nested bullets) is its own item routed by the header, and a header
line starts a new list even with no blank line before it. Each item is still
judged alone, with its own markers and whole-item forms, so
bulk linking (several `@route:id` items) and bulk completion (one `!note:id` per item)
work. The draft-wide `@@route` form routes otherwise-unrouted items across a blank-line batch; the `%t` directive marks the draft's first item as a template that declares and expands before parsing. One staged planner
(`CaptureBatchPlanner`) runs the items in order, so each item sees the edits planned
before it (insertion points, block-ID checks, Pomodoro lineup numbers) exactly as
sequential captures would, and any item's failure rolls the whole draft back. JSON
output puts the first result in the legacy top-level fields plus an ordered `captures`
array (`capture-parse` adds `items`), and human output numbers items `1/N`. Bob Mac
Capture still submits one `bob capture` call: the preview stacks items under a count,
the footer stays **Capture** instead of a single-item verb such as Link, Start, Close,
Complete, or Queue, the notification is titled with the count, and Shift-Return in the
`!` picker appends a blank line plus `!` for the next completion. Docs and code also say
"batch" for any capture's staged writes, even a single item's.

### Capture {#capture}

One `bob capture` run over one draft: its arguments, piped stdin, or Bob Mac Capture's
panel, which submits the whole draft as exactly one `bob capture` call and hides only
once bob reports success (see [Bob Mac Capture Is A Thin Client Of bob](../develop/decisions.md#mac-capture-is-a-thin-client)). bob splits
the draft into capture items, each a parent line plus optional authored child bullets,
and each item's markers decide what it does. That is far more than GTD inbox capture: an
item may create a task (default `mac_inbox.md`, an [Inbox File](#inbox-file)), bullet, sub-bullet,
project note (a [Project Note Capture](#project-note-capture)), a note in a [Notebook](#notebook), a notebook, or
record note (a [Record Note](#record-note) in an [Album Note](#album-note), see `docs/records.md`); queue a bare public URL as a background reference job, never touching
the network; link, start, complete, or relate existing tasks (`@route:id`, `!note:id`,
`&`, `*`); or start, adjust, shift, or close today's Pomodoro (`=`, `+N`, `++N`, `x`).
bob plans every edit against in-memory snapshots of the target notes and today's daily
note, then writes all or nothing: a note changed on disk since planning, or any failed
item, aborts the run and rolls back anything already written. `--dry-run` runs the same
planner without writing; the app's live preview is `bob capture --dry-run`, with `--no-clip`
unless Bob reports a `%c` clip directive. An
unfinished picker query (`:dee`, `/fix`, `!fix`, `&`, `Call the bank +`) is refused,
never captured as prose. The editor-facing `capture-*` companion commands are not
captures, nor are `bob gkeep pull`, `bob ref create`, or Obsidian keymaps. A draft with
two or more items is a [Bulk Capture](#bulk-capture); the grammar lives in `docs/capture.md`.

### Capture Alias {#capture-alias}

*Aliases: sigil alias.*

A keystroke substitution in Bob Mac Capture's editor: an easy-to-reach key that the app
swaps for the [Capture](#capture) sigil it stands for, only where that sigil would act at the
caret by opening its picker or filling a close slot. bob decides every one
([Bob Mac Capture Is A Thin Client Of bob](../develop/decisions.md#mac-capture-is-a-thin-client)). The app sends the post-key draft and caret
to `bob capture-rewrite --cursor`, which answers with rule `expand_sigil_alias` (summary
`Typed ^ for .`), and the app applies that one edit natively, so Undo restores the typed
key. The aliases:

- `.` → `^` right after `@route` (`@errands.` → `@errands^`); `;` → `:` there, and as a
  whole item (Task Link picker). In a [Project Note Capture](#project-note-capture), a first-level `- .` or
  `- ;` opens the Move picker and `- ^.` gives `- ^^`.
- `.` → `@` after body text and a space or tab, wherever a bare `@` opens route
  completion and the item is not already routed (`Buy milk .` → `Buy milk @`).
- `.` → `&` and `;` → `*` after text or a marker and a space or tab, where a bare `&` /
  `*` opens the Depends On / Blocks picker; once the item is routed, `.` gives `&`
  wherever Depends On opens (`Buy milk @foo:bar .` → `Buy milk @foo:bar &`;
  `Buy milk .` stays `@`).
- `,` → `+` wherever the Parent Task picker would open (`@cash,` → `@cash+`); glued to a
  complete `@route+id` target, it inserts ` +` for the next pick.
- `/` → `#` wherever a `#` menu would open (task type, section, Pomodoro name,
  wikilink heading, and the rest). Never at a line start, glued to a word, or after
  another `/`; `/` stays literal where it is already field text (`=/`, `[[folder/`).
- `\` → `%` wherever a bare `%` would open the directive menu (`Buy milk \` →
  `Buy milk %`). Never at a line start, glued to a word, or after another `\`.
- `-` → `~` inside an `x=` past token (`x=2-` → `x=2~`); a spaced `-` stays literal.
- `=` → `~` after a space or tab where the Links To relation picker would open, while
  `~=` / `~~=` flip to `~~` / `~` ([Relation Equals Alias And Flips](../develop/decisions.md#relation-equals-alias-and-flips)).
- `x` / `s` → `!` / `*` (complete / park) when the lowercase letter ends a close
  selection: `xx` → `x!`, `+2 xs` → `+2 x*`, `2xx` → `2x!`, `@r:id=xx` → `@r:id=x!`.

Open pickers honour bob's `action_continuation_aliases`: `,` acts as `+` in the lone-`+`
Parent Task picker, and `.` acts as `^` in the `- ^` Move picker. In the relation picker
and label card, `=` flips direction like `~`. The only app-local alias is a blank
draft's `\` → `/`, which opens Go To. Each alias can be escaped: by Undo; by a fast
second `=` or the spaced `.`/`;` fallbacks (350 ms), which type one literal (`===`
gives `==`; `..` and `;;` give one `.` or `;`); by a second `\`/`/` at any speed; or
by Space or Escape on the still-empty picker the alias opened. Aliases that change
meaning (`x`/`s`, and `-` in `x=`) hold later edits and
Return until bob answers. On a timeout the key stays literal and Return is dropped ("Bob
did not answer; press Return again"). An older bob leaves every alias literal.

Aliases exist only while typing. `bob capture`, `capture-parse`, paste, and piped stdin
keep the text, so a pasted `Buy milk .` captures a dot and `xx` closes nothing. Template
drafts and `#"…"` exact-name literals are never rewritten. Rewrites in the same lane
that edit an existing marker are not aliases: the block-ID separator toggle
(`@route:id^` → `@route^id`, or a glued `.` toggle (`@route:id.` ↔ `@route^id`, `@route+id.` → `@route^id`), or the glued `,` switch (`@route:id,` → `@route+id`)),
the glued `~`/`=` relation direction flip, the `|` label
attach, `@@` absorption, and the `@@route` collapse (`@@cash/` → `@cash#`).
None of these is a capture alias either: the Mac's "Capture
alias" hotkey (Settings › Hotkey's global `Command-\`), a frontmatter or
`project_name_aliases` route alias, a wikilink `|alias`, a deprecated tag spelling
(`#offclock`), the bare owner alias `^route:id`, Tab's `--` → `—` snippet, or the
close-list comma (`x1` then `2` → `x1,2`). See bob-cli `docs/capture.md`
(`bob capture-rewrite`, "Sigil alias") and Bob Mac Capture's `docs/keyboard.md` and
`docs/capture-panel.md`.

`bob capture-rewrite --cursor` also returns `sigil_alias_tip`, proved by running the
forward rewrite; Bob Mac Capture shows it as a fading "Next time" row in the list or
picker the sigil opened.

### Command Mode {#command-mode}

*Aliases: Bob Command Mode, command sheet.*

The `bob-command-mode` Obsidian desktop plugin's bottom command sheet: a fuzzy finder
for running `bob` commands without leaving the vault. With Obsidian's Vim mode on, `:`
in normal mode opens it, because the vault vimrc (`obsidian_vimrc.md`) maps
`nnoremap : :bob_command<CR>` onto `exmap bob_command obcommand bob-command-mode:open`;
**Bob: Command mode** in the command palette opens it in any view. Its rows come from
bob's hidden, versioned `bob __catalog` handshake, so the binary, never the plugin,
decides which commands, arguments, and write policies exist, and excluded commands are
refused. An empty query shows RECENT runs, FOR THIS NOTE rows, FROM CLIPBOARD URLs, and
one group per catalog section. `Enter` runs a row, `Tab` enters argument mode,
`Shift+Enter` previews, `Ctrl+Enter` runs now or applies a preview, and a trailing `?`
shows help; reports stream into an output pager. Each run spawns `bob` directly, with no
shell, and its record and output stay host-local under
`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/bob-cli/command-mode/runs/`, never in the vault.
Writers run one at a time and only after every open Markdown editor saves; a writer
without a preview asks first on a confirm card, while reads run in parallel. Catalog
rows that need no arguments, preview, or confirmation also appear in the command palette
as `Bob: <title>`, and sibling plugins run commands through the same engine
(`api.commandMode`). In Bob, "command mode" never means Vim's normal mode or its `:`
command line: `g:` in normal mode, or `::` in the sheet, still opens Vim's ex line, and
Vim-shaped input such as `:%s/a/b/` or `:42` is routed there. Not a [Capture](#capture):
free-text `bob capture TEXT` is refused here, and a capture draft's leading `:` opens
the task-link picker instead. Not the SASE TUI's command-mode panel. See
`docs/guides/run-bob-from-obsidian.md`.

### Day Strip {#day-strip}

*Aliases: day stats.*

The [Stats Strip](#stats-strip) of a daily note: the read-only daily Stats summary at the top
of the `bob-plan` block on canonical daily notes, above the badges, in Live
Preview and Reading view, or wherever a `bob-day-stats` fence embeds it. Its contents: five
LABEL-value facts, each numeric one over a quiet `typical` line (the median of
the seven days before, with a ▲/▼/= mark once the day is finished), then a
[Root Parent](#root-parent) lane and a [Task Type](#task-type) lane, each a legend over a
full-width bar, shown together or one at a time by the bars switch on
the top lane row beside `so far · HH:MM`; the last bar separates it from the badges. bob
owns every value, and it never writes the note. `## Pomodoros` no longer
repeats its total. Facts and the bars open the [Stats Dash](#stats-dash) with the day
pinned. "Day stats" in UI copy (`Toggle Day stats`, `stats.day_strip`).
Not the [Morning GTD Review Footer](#morning-gtd-review-footer).

### Event Ack {#event-ack}

*Aliases: ack, unacked, event acknowledgement, gcal ack.*

Bob's one-time review answer for an external Google Calendar event that will
land as an [Event Task](#event-task). A live `gcal.ack` receipt or any persisted
nonempty private event note counts, including note text later cleared; a
series note covers its future instances. Until answered, an open Event Task
carries Bob's `#unacked` warning tag. Removing that exact tag is itself an
acknowledgement. The review is a reminder, not an RSVP or a sync gate: Bob
still writes eligible Event Tasks, and never writes to Google. See
`docs/gcal-acks.md`.

### Event Task {#event-task}

*Aliases: event row, calendar task.*

A checkbox `#task` row inside a canonical daily note's `## Events` section,
whose description begins with a local `**HHMM-HHMM**` span. Hand-written
rows qualify. Its `[root:: NOTE]` attributes meeting time to an area or
project, and a Pomodoro Task Link under the daily note's ledger records the
session. `#off`, `#on`, or an inherited area/project `offclock:` through
`[root::]` decides whether the session that links it is an
[Off-Clock Pomodoro](#off-clock-pomodoro), so its `[root::]` attributes those minutes. A synced MEET Event Task can match a root note's `offclock_types` list.
On timed close, Bob compares the span with the session's start and
close times: a meeting that ended inside is completed, one still running
stays In Progress and carried, and one not started or ended before the
session is deferred. Explicit numbered selections take precedence; wildcard
completion and parking do not select a not-started meeting. See
`docs/reference/vault-format.md` and `docs/capture.md`.

An Event Task is a daily-note residence exception beside `^gtd`. See the
[Area Note](#area-note), [Pomodoro](#pomodoro), [Task Link](#task-link), and [Root Parent](#root-parent).

### Gmail Task {#gmail-task}

*Aliases: gmail task, email task.*

A task wired to a saved Gmail thread: a checkbox `#task` whose own line, or a direct link-only child bullet, carries a wikilink to a saved mail note (frontmatter `type: "[[mail]]"` or a string `gmail_thread_id`). The link is the wire — the task's residence never matters, one thread may wire several Gmail Tasks, and any task status qualifies. Born from `bob gmail sync` filing a labelled thread (one task row routed by its routing label, falling back to the Gmail [Inbox File](#inbox-file)), a [Capture](#capture) whose Gmail URL swaps to the labelled link, **Bob Mail: Task from this email**, or any hand-written task line that links a mail note. Every _open_ Gmail Task watches its thread: your counted send holds it with exact `#awaiting_reply` plus one `[scheduled::]` nudge date, and a reply or bounce lifts the hold ([Awaiting A Gmail Reply Is A Tagged Schedule Hold](../develop/decisions.md#gmail-reply-wait-is-a-tagged-hold)). Its row wears the display-only reply badge, no-reply pill, and also-replied tooltip pip (`docs/mail-link-marks.md`); with the cursor anywhere on the row — or on a link-only `[[note#^id]]` Task Link bullet pointing at it — the vault's Meta+Enter `bob-navigation-hotkeys:open-reference-pdf-in-highlights` command opens the thread in the browser from the mail note's `gmail_url` via bob-mail's `api.mailOpen` (with the vim normal-mode `<M-CR>` / `<M-Enter>` mapping as fallback), and a muted `⌘↵ Gmail` chip on the cursor row shows exactly when that delivery path is live. The gesture is read-only: it never writes, stamps [Task Freshness](#task-freshness), or advances the `]s` walk. Not the mail note itself (the saved snapshot), not an [Event Task](#event-task), and not a Pomodoro [Task Link](#task-link) to the task; `#awaiting_reply` is a hold a Gmail Task may wear, never what makes it one. A task that merely mentions a thread in a nested note bullet is not a Gmail Task and does not watch. See `docs/gmail.md#watch`.

### Inbox File {#inbox-file}

*Aliases: inbox note.*

A Bob vault Markdown file whose tasks await triage: `inbox.md` at the vault root, or an
[Area Note](#area-note) whose frontmatter `parent` resolves to `inbox.md` (today `mac_inbox.md`,
`gkeep_inbox.md`, and `gmail_inbox.md`). Only direct area children count, and the filename is irrelevant:
a [Project Note](#project-note) filed under one (`gkeep_gdocs_inbox_dump`) or an untyped child
(`inbox_overflow`) is not an inbox file. Classification reads live frontmatter on every
gesture, and `inbox.md` counts by design though it holds no `#task` lines today. By
default, `bob capture` and Bob Mac Capture file new tasks in `mac_inbox.md`,
`bob gkeep pull` drains Google Keep into `gkeep_inbox.md`, and `bob gmail sync`
files `bob`-labelled threads into the area/project named by their routing label, falling back to `gmail_inbox.md` when none or an invalid one is present. New tasks carry no `fresh`
stamp, so most surface for triage in the NEW tier of the `]s` walk. On an open task in
an inbox file, every non-closing Ctrl+Shift+P answer and Alt+N ask where the task goes
just before writing; a Ctrl+Shift+Enter link on the task line asks first, so the
Pomodoro picker suggests the destination's type, while its unlink asks just before
writing; apply the action in place, then move the task without following it; the route
picker never offers another inbox
file, and `⇧↵` applies the answer without moving. Ctrl+Shift+M also moves it, following
it to the destination. A capture that changes an existing inbox task's
status asks the same question in Bob Mac Capture's route card, and bob moves the task
in that capture's batch (`bob capture -i/--inbox-route`); otherwise a closed task
leaves through `bob task archive`. The current
inbox files set `ready_cap: off`. bob-plugins and `docs/projects.md` ("Inbox routing")
say "inbox note" (`api.inboxRoute.isInboxNote`); that is not a Google Keep inbox note,
the Keep item `bob gkeep` drains. bob-cli capture's `INBOX_FILE` constant and
`kind: inbox` target mean only `mac_inbox.md`, the default capture route.

### Keep Streak {#keep-streak}

*Aliases: keeps.*

The count of consecutive due reviews at which a human confirmed a task as written
on its current rung, stored as `[keeps:: N]` (1–999; absence means 0) right after
the task's `fresh`/`refresh` fields. Due keeps count on every rung — WIP on the
PENDING tier, Next on the NEXT tier, Ready and P-levels on ROTTEN or scheduled
TICKLER — once per review through the single keep helper; a keep on an unblock
tickler (`returned_by: unblocked`) leaves the streak unchanged. Any rung change
clears it, whoever makes it: human lane and priority writers stamp, and
reconcile's lane raises strip it in the same line write (`Unblock` back to Ready
preserves it); hand edits stay unobserved, and automation otherwise never touches
it. At the rung's allowance the next due confirmation opens the [Task Decay](#task-decay)
card instead of stamping; see [Task Decay Is One Ladder](../develop/decisions.md#task-decay-is-one-ladder),
[Unblocked Tasks Resurface As Ticklers](../develop/decisions.md#unblocked-tasks-resurface-as-ticklers), and
[Task Freshness](#task-freshness).

### Leaf Project {#leaf-project}

# Leaf Project

*Requested · project*

A [Project Note](#project-note) that is not its own [Root Parent](#root-parent), meaning a sub-project
at any depth whose `parent` walk meets another project before any
[Area Note](#area-note) and that does not set `root: true` itself. A
[Top-Level Project](#top-level-project), a `root: true` project, and an orphan project (nothing
above it) are roots, never leaves. "Leaf" names the reporting role, not tree
position: a leaf project may have sub-projects. Leafness is derived from the
note tree at gesture time, never stored, and a task's `[root::]` field never
changes it. Closing the task behind a leaf project's last live
[Task Link](#task-link) in today's Pomodoros offers the project's ready tasks as
keep-moving [Successor Offer](#successor-offer)s, which are never dependents (see
`docs/task-dependencies.md` §12.15).

### Mac Menu Bar Pomodoro Indicator {#mac-menu-bar-pomodoro-indicator}

*Aliases: mac pom.*

The Hammerspoon status item in the macOS menu bar on Bryan's MacBook that shows the
current Pomodoro at a glance. It is a read-only consumer of
`bob pomodoro --show-stale --worked --last`: it re-syncs when today's daily note changes and
polls every 60 seconds (15 seconds without the file watcher), on wake and unlock, from
its Refresh menu item, and once when the countdown crosses zero; it ticks the countdown
locally in between and never writes the vault. A running session reads
`NAME (50m) · 🍅 12:34`, where NAME is the Pomodoro's ` — NAME`. Each known,
non-exempt theme component prefixes NAME with a colored `■` using the hue
reported by `bob themes list -a -f json`; unknown or exempt themes and a failed
catalog call have no swatch. An unnamed session with linked tasks shows its
derived home label (`sase (50m) · 🍅 12:34`);
`UNTITLED` only appears when there is nothing to derive. Once overdue, a `→ HH:MM` stop time joins the title and the `+MM:SS` count
turns red; from ten minutes overdue the count becomes an `OVERDUE` badge flashing red
at 1 Hz, and `--show-stale` holds it there rather than letting it read as idle. Without
a session it shows today's worked total `<H>h<M>m` (bob's `[WORKED <minutes>m]`, closed
Pomodoros only) in green with no tomato, flashing as a green pill on Fibonacci-spaced
10-second steps that append `φ Nm`, re-anchored when the label reappears or the Mac
wakes or unlocks; after a closed session the title leads with `⇥ HH:MM · ` (the end of
today's last closed Pomodoro, from bob's `[LAST HHMM-HHMM]` token) in the ordinary
foreground, and the mark never flashes; empty output falls back to `NO POMODORO`. A failed or unparsable run
hides the item. It is neither the `bob pomodoro tmux` status line nor Bob Mac Capture's
menu-bar item. It lives in the linked `chezmoi` repo under `home/dot_hammerspoon/`
(`init.lua` runtime, `pomodoro_countdown.lua` presentation policy); that repo's README
"Pomodoro menu bar" section is its spec, so coordinate `bob pomodoro` output changes
with it.

### Merged Pomodoro {#merged-pomodoro}

*Aliases: merged pomodoro, composite pomodoro, base type.*

A [Pomodoro](#pomodoro) whose ` — NAME` holds two or more [Task Type](#task-type) components, for
example `BUILD + FIX + READ`. The first component is the base type, the one the
others were merged into; the rest are merged-in types, in name order. With a
configured vocabulary, non-type components are labels and never count; without one,
each component is a type unless it is an inventory label. `BOB + BUILD` is not merged
when BOB is a label, and a container such as `LATER` is not merged.

Landing into an existing open [Pomodoro](#pomodoro) merges instead of retyping: when a
[Task Link](#task-link) lands in an entry of another type, the destination gains ` + TYPE` and
no task field is written. The Obsidian link, move, and successor pickers merge on
Enter and retype only on Alt+Enter. Creating a new entry from a typed or picked name
retypes the task landing in it, so the new name already agrees with its link; a
container name types nothing.

[Capture](#capture) `=*` merges planned entries into a survivor, `=/` splits merged-in
types out into new planned entries below the source, and Obsidian Ctrl+S splits the
selected entry the same way: two types split immediately, three or more prompt for
the types to move.

At close, `settle_closed` names the closed session from the labels plus exactly the
types of its worked links, in entry order. It appends missing worked types in catalog
spelling and substitutes in place when one type is removed and one is added;
single-type names can rename. The continuation first sheds unsupported merged types,
keeping the base when needed, then agrees with its carried links so it is an
`agree_entry` fixed point. Open entry names stay in agreement through writers, the
close settle, and reconcile ([Open Pomodoro Names Follow Task Links](../develop/decisions.md#open-pomodoro-names-follow-task-links)).
A name that normalizes to MEET is never merged, split, settled, shed, or renamed.

This is not a container, not a Pomodoro home, and not a D6 rename.

### Morning GTD Review Footer {#morning-gtd-review-footer}

*Aliases: review footer.*

The `s` member of the [Walker Footer](#walker-footer): the bob-ledger-tools item in Obsidian's desktop status bar, shown while the review walk is the active bracket walk, that keeps the morning GTD
review — the tiered `]s` walk over the shared [Task Freshness](#task-freshness) queue — in view
while you work through it. It answers three questions at a glance: how much is still
due, where the cursor sits in the walk, and whether the commitment tiers are done
(after them come ROTTEN upkeep, which is fine to stop partway, and the POST
closeout). Off a queue row it reads `⟳ Review N due · K commitments` (or
`Commitments done` / `Upkeep budget met`); the hint becomes the `Alt+P` preview
when the cursor is on an open task with a priority, and stays `]] next` otherwise.
On a queue row it reads `⟳ Review r/N · TIER i/M` plus that row's detail and, when the row has a
recommended roll, the `Alt+P` preview in the hint slot (for example
`Alt+P roll P2 1/1`); on TICK rows that preview renders as a tinted answer chip. The other nonempty tier
groups follow in walk order, then the `✓ upkeep/budget today` meter. To fit the
status bar it uses short tier labels — `WIP` for PENDING (WIP is an official alias of
the Pending status), `RECUR` for RECURRING, `TICKS` for TICKLER — explained in its
tooltip. Each group, and the current tier's context, wears that tier's own color; a
hairline divider separates the commitment groups from ROTTEN and POST; and as space
runs out it drops groups from the end of the walk (marking the cut with `…`), then
detail, hint, and meter, except on TICK rows, where the meter goes before the `Alt+P` chip.
Clicking jumps to the next due task like `]s`. It is a read-only projection: it never
stamps or changes tasks, its numbers are queue positions rather than progress, and it
hides when Tasks is unavailable. When nothing is due, it reads `⟳ Review clear · ✓ N today` — "clear" describes the current eligible queue, not the week's commitments — keeping the `Alt+P` preview when the cursor is
on an open task with a priority.
`]s` notices and
`bob freshness list` keep full tier names, and dashboard ROTTEN chips fold TICKLER
into ROTTEN where the footer splits them; see [Review Walk Is Tiered With Daily Lane Review](../develop/decisions.md#review-walk-is-tiered). While review commitments are due off-`s`, a quiet dot on the selector's `s` letter marks them.

### Notebook {#notebook}

*Aliases: notebook note.*

A Bob vault Markdown file with frontmatter `type: "[[notebook]]"` that keeps a
named collection of related notes (observations, explanations, ideas, logs)
without the obligations of a new [Area Note](#area-note) or [Project Note](#project-note). Its body is
note bullets, optionally grouped under `##` sections below an H1 title; each
bullet may carry nested detail, a `[created::]` stamp, and a stable `^id`. It
never holds a `#task` or any checkbox, so it is never a task's residence, a
Pomodoro home, a Ready lane, a review item, or a [Root Parent](#root-parent); root, clock,
and type walks pass through it to the nearest area or project above it (its
owner).

Its single `parent` names an area note, a project note, or another notebook, and
the chain always reaches an area or project. A one-line `summary:` states what
belongs there. Every area or project lists the notebooks beneath it, down to the
next root parent, in a machine-owned `## Notebooks` catalog that
`bob notebooks sync` maintains: its content is bob's, its position is Bryan's.
`bob notebooks list` and `bob notebooks check` report the tree, counts, and
contract findings.

In [Capture](#capture), the destination decides. On a notebook route, `@nb` adds a
top-level note, `@nb#section` adds one to that `##` section (exact match,
created on demand), `@nb^id` or `@nb#section^id` adds a named note, `@nb+id`
adds a child of the note bullet `^id`, and a draft-wide `@@nb` sends every
unrouted item there as a note. In a route-only `@nb` list, a first-level
`- #Section` bullet selects a section and its nested one-line bullets become
notes in that section; plain first-level siblings remain top-region notes.
`@parent^id@ %n <summary>` creates a notebook with the same section-bullet
behavior, while a bare `%n` stays a Pomodoro note. Task-only markers are
refused with a rewrite to the owner's route.

Not a [Reference Note](#reference-note), a [Record Note](#record-note) or [Album Note](#album-note), a [Task Drawer](#task-drawer),
a [Period Note](#period-note), the Pomodoro note `%n` writes, or an Obsidian folder. An album
and a notebook are siblings under an area or project; neither can parent the
other. See
`docs/notebooks.md` and [A Notebook Route Writes Notes; `@@` Stays Draft-Wide](../develop/decisions.md#notebook-routes-write-notes).

### Off-Clock Pomodoro {#off-clock-pomodoro}

*Aliases: off-clock session, untracked pomodoro, untracked session.*

A [Pomodoro](#pomodoro) whose time Bob records but keeps off the work clock — lunch, the gym, school pickup. Its timespan carries `[off:: Nm]` where a worked session carries `[t:: Nm]`: `- [x] (**1200-1300** [off:: 60m]) — MEET`. A session goes off the clock exactly when it keeps at least one [Task Link](#task-link) and every one resolves off-clock: `#off` (deprecated `#offclock`, `#off-clock`, `#untracked`), an inherited area/project `offclock: true`, or a matching `offclock_types` list on the nearest policy note; `#on` and `offclock: false` remain overrides; an unlinked session, an unresolved link, or one on-clock link keeps the whole session worked. Writers decide when they write the span (starts, closes, and `bob gcal sync` for an off-clock [Event Task](#event-task)); a closed row's key is history, and later tag, type, root, or note-policy edits are reported, never applied. An ended off-clock [Event Task](#event-task) nobody started — tagged or inherited — settles into one on the next `bob task reconcile`. Worked, Sessions, `bob pomodoro --worked`, and the [Day Strip](#day-strip) facts leave it out; its [Root Parent](#root-parent) still receives its minutes. The Off-clock and Total clocks of `bob stats -k` and the [Stats Dash](#stats-dash) count it, grouped by [Root Parent](#root-parent) like any session. Drawn dashed; `◌` in text. A bare closed `(**HHMM-HHMM**)` row is an older off-clock session counted by its span. Not a `()` placeholder, a Stats day before tracking began (`not_tracked`), or the tracked-task mark on a `#task` row. See [Off-Clock Note Defaults Filter By Task Type](../develop/decisions.md#off-clock-note-defaults-filter-by-task-type).

### Period Note {#period-note}

*Aliases: weekly note, quarterly note, yearly note, all_time.*

A Bob vault note for one period above the day, in whole ISO weeks:

- `YYYY/YYYY-Www.md`: a Mon–Sun ISO week, filed under its ISO week-year;
- `YYYY/YYYY-Qn.md`: 13 ISO weeks (W01–13, W14–26, W27–39, W40–52/53);
- `YYYY.md`: an ISO week-year;
- `all_time.md`: the singleton.

Each `parent` is the next period up (a daily note's is its week, a year's is
`all_time`, and `all_time`'s is `org`), so the tree is also an exact partition of
days. bob creates them, create-only and one week ahead (`bob periods ensure`).

Each opens with a [Stats Strip](#stats-strip) and a live parts table that summarizes every child
with its Headline or the root parents it mostly went to. It then holds:

- Bryan's `Intentions`, `Outcomes`, or `Theme`;
- a `## Review` that an agent may draft only through `bob periods draft`, while it
  is empty or still unedited;
- Bryan's `## Reflection`;
- a folded `[!agent]` callout with the complete, versioned drafting instructions.

Period notes hold no task rows. Monthly notes are retired: months are a Stats
grouping, not a note level. Not a daily note, an [Area Note](#area-note), or a
[Project Note](#project-note).

### Pomodoro {#pomodoro}

A Pomodoro is a column-0 checkbox item under `## Pomodoros` in an Obsidian daily file, representing one timed session, on the clock (`[t::]`) or off it (`[off::]`, an [Off-Clock Pomodoro](#off-clock-pomodoro)). Its body is either a timespan such as `(**0920-0950** [t:: 30m])` or an empty `()` placeholder; an optional ` — NAME` suffix (em dash plus ALL-CAPS name) makes it a named Pomodoro. Past Pomodoros are closed with timespans, current Pomodoros are open with timespans, and planned Pomodoros are open placeholders. Child bullets log the session's work, usually with a task link. On a sub-bullet, `N<ctrl+shift+m>` moves it and the next N siblings into another open Pomodoro, or into a new named one below.

### Project Note {#project-note}

*Aliases: prj note.*

A Bob vault Markdown file with frontmatter `type: "[[project]]"` that holds a project's
context and work. Its [Project Task](#project-task) (`^prj`) states the completion criteria and
represents the project's overall status; ordinary tasks describe work toward that
outcome. A closed project remains a project note if its `^prj` task is archived. An
`offclock: true|false` key sets the clock default for tasks on the root walk
beneath it (see [Off-Clock Follows Tag Then Note Default](../develop/decisions.md#off-clock-follows-tag-then-note-default)). `offclock_types` sets the clock off only for tasks whose effective type is listed and wins when both keys are present (see [Off-Clock Note Defaults Filter By Task Type](../develop/decisions.md#off-clock-note-defaults-filter-by-task-type)). See
`docs/projects.md`.

### Project Note Capture {#project-note-capture}

*Aliases: project capture, project-note capture.*

A [Capture](#capture) item whose route marker is sealed with a trailing `@`, `@<route>^<id>@` or
`@<route>:<id>@` (optionally followed by `#<pomodoro>`), so it creates a brand-new
[Project Note](#project-note) instead of a task. With `%n`, the `^` seal creates a [Notebook](#notebook)
instead (parent area, project, or notebook; the item text becomes its `summary`). The marker may lead the item or trail any of its
lines. bob writes `<route>_<id>.md` at the vault root (each `-` in the ID becomes `_`)
with `parent: "[[<route>]]"`, `type: "[[project]]"`, `status: wip`, and the
`template: "[[new_project]]"` line, in the same shape as the Obsidian **Create project
note from task** command, which instead promotes an existing task. The item's parent
text becomes the [Project Task](#project-task) line `- [ ] #task #prj <text> #hide ^prj` (`[?]`
once the item resolves a schedule), which is never linked. `<route>.md` must already
be an area or non-terminal project note, a target note that already exists or is staged
refuses the capture, and the same batch lists it in the parent's `## Projects`
catalog.

The sigil before the ID picks the form. The `^` (create) form links only the item's
explicit `:` bullets. The `:` (offer) form creates the same note, then offers its open,
unhidden, not-yet-linked `## Tasks` rows as [Successor Offer](#successor-offer)s of the new `^prj`,
linking none until picked with `-p` (Bob Mac Capture's Pull-In card). A `#<pomodoro>`
after the seal names the Pomodoro those links land under, created on demand, and is
refused when the item has nothing to link or offer.

First-level bullets mirror the new note
([Capture Bullets Mirror The Task Block](../develop/decisions.md#capture-bullets-mirror-the-task-block)). Each becomes a `## Tasks` row: a
trailing ` :<id>` names it, makes it Next, and adds its [Task Link](#task-link) under the
Pomodoro its type places (or the `#<pomodoro>` one), while ` ^<id>` only names it. An
ALL-CAPS bullet with nested notes becomes a `## Title Case` section instead. A bullet
that is only `^<id>` or `:<id>` moves an existing open top-level task out of the parent
note (`:` also links it), and `- ^^` chooses several from a Move card before writing.
The new note, the moved blocks, and today's ledger write in one all-or-nothing batch.

`%c`, `--clip`, `=<X>` and `=x` session suffixes, `!`, and `@@` declarations are
refused, and the retired `+` seals (`@route^id+`, `@route:id+`) teach the `@` spelling.
Not `@route^id` (an ordinary task with a block ID), `@route:id` (a task linked into a
Pomodoro), `@route+id` (a note under an existing task), or record-note capture
(`@dir/^stem`). `capture-parse` reports mode `project_note`, or `pomodoro_project_note`
once the item links a task. See `docs/capture.md` ("Project notes") and
`docs/reference/capture-syntax.md` ("Project captures").

### Project Task {#project-task}

*Aliases: prj task.*

The single project-level `#task` checkbox in a [Project Note](#project-note), identified by the exact
trailing block ID `^prj`. Its description states what must be true for the project to be
complete. The `^prj` line carries the project's date (inline `scheduled`) and dep links
(its Depends-On line); while either blocks it, every open task in the note is Blocked
and tagged `#prj_is_blocked`. `bob projects sync` maps checked to `status: done`,
canceled to `status: canceled`, and reopening a terminal project to `status: wip`; an
open nonterminal project's status is preserved. New lines include `#prj`; legacy lines
without that tag remain recognized. See `docs/projects.md` and
[Projects Block Their Tasks From The ^prj Line](../develop/decisions.md#projects-block-from-prj-line).

### Record Note {#record-note}

A durable item in an [Album Note](#album-note)'s folder, with frontmatter `type: "[[record]]"`
and `parent` linking to its album. Its schema-defined fields hold facts about the item;
optional `## Notes` bullets hold observations, with dates when the album enables dated
notes. The album's generated index catalogs its record notes. Capture can create or
update one with `@album/` or `@album/<stem>`; `bob records new|update` writes the same
record-note format and `bob records check` validates it. Record notes are not notebooks,
references, or tasks. See `docs/records.md`.

### Reference Note {#reference-note}

*Aliases: ref note.*

A Bob vault Markdown file with frontmatter `type: "[[ref]]"` for a particular piece of
external reference material, such as a book, article, or captured conversation. It
gathers source links plus notes or highlights. It holds no open tasks. It shows its
reading task (`#task #ref`, living in the parent area, project, or inbox note's
`## Tasks`) through the managed embed `![[<residence>#^<id>]]` one blank line below the
H1. Frontmatter `parent` is projected from where that task lives (a `done/` archive maps
to that file's `parent:`). Annotation follow-up tasks default to the parent note. A
frozen in-note `^ref` tracker is the legacy v1 shape. Highlights sync generates this
form; legacy notes may lack the task. See `docs/highlights-ref-sync.md` and
[Reference Task](#reference-task).

### Reference Task {#reference-task}

*Aliases: ref task.*

The single source-level `#task` checkbox that tracks progress through the external
material of a [Reference Note](#reference-note). A modern reading task lives in the reference's
parent (area, project, or inbox) note, identified by the trailing block ID
`^ref-<slug>` — with a `-vN` suffix for rereads (`^ref-<root-slug>-vN`, alias
`Title (vN)`) — while the reference note itself carries a managed embed pointing at
it. A legacy in-note `^ref` tracker is still recognized. In Highlights-generated
notes the task links to the PDF: `[ ]` means `ready`, `[*]` means `next`, `[/]` means
`wip`, `[x]`/`[X]` means `read`, and `[-]` means `abandoned`. Highlights sync
reconciles this with note and PDF status. New lines include `#ref`; legacy lines
without that tag remain recognized. Follow-up tasks track separate work. See
`docs/highlights-ref-sync.md`.

### Root Parent {#root-parent}

A task's root parent is derived at read time from its note chain, unless its
explicit `[root:: NOTE]` field names the note where Bob should begin that walk.
The field is reporting-only: it attributes Pomodoro time and task metrics as if
the checkbox lived in the named note, while the checkbox stays in its original
file. Archive and reference wrappers are walked through. An area at any depth,
a project marked `root: true`, or the outermost project names itself as the root;
a subproject without `root: true` groups under its nearest root project, or the
outermost project when none is marked. A missing, invalid, or duplicate root
field falls back to the task's own note. A walk with no area or project is
`@unfiled`; unlinked Pomodoros remain `@unlinked`. The synthetic `GTD` bucket
(`@daily`) and named review buckets are retired. Daily review time is the time
attributed to tasks in, or rooted at, `gtd`; each daily note's `^gtd` row
carries `[root:: gtd]`.

Root parents are derived from the current note tree and never stored as a
separate status. `rollup:` no longer exists. The [Day Strip](#day-strip)'s root-parent
bar and the default [Stats Dash](#stats-dash) view group by it; Stats JSON calls the
dimension `root_parent`. It is not the nearest home (`project`), a top-level
area, or a [Task Type](#task-type); see `docs/pomodoro-homes.md`.

### Rotten Log {#rotten-log}

*Aliases: keep log.*

A task-local history of rung events, stored as a `🥀 **ROTTEN LOG**` direct child
with newest-first entries `*YYYY-MM-DD* — <body>`. Every counted keep, Stay, step,
and drop writes exactly one entry in the same transaction as its stamp, with one
undo; a blank reason always logs `🤷 no reason given`, and Esc writes nothing. A
counted keep logs `<reason> · kept N× in <Rung>` (`at` for P-levels; WIP, Next,
and Ready use `in`), N the [Keep Streak](#keep-streak) after that keep; a Stay logs `<reason>
· stayed in <Rung> after N keeps`; a step logs `🍂 <from> → <to> · after N keeps`
(`🍂 rolled again at P4 · after N keeps` at the bottom); a drop logs `🍂 <Rung> →
dropped · after N keeps` plus the existing Cancel Log entry. WIP keeps log here,
never in the [Work Log](#work-log); freshness gestures never write or prompt for the Work
Log. The decay card's header derives per-rung keep tallies from these entries at
read time. The entry count never resets, is never stored as a field, and nothing
reads it to change decay, lanes, Today, schedule, priority, or
[Task Freshness](#task-freshness). NEW, early, same-day repeat, Today-linked, PROJECTS,
recurring, checklist, closed, and unblock-tickler keeps never prompt and never
write it; deferrals and rewords stay in the [Schedule Log](#schedule-log). `bob capture`,
Rust, hooks, randomize, and seed never write it. There is no backfill: keeps
before rollout leave no entries. See [Task Decay Is One Ladder](../develop/decisions.md#task-decay-is-one-ladder).

### Schedule Log {#schedule-log}

When the `<ctrl+shift+p>` Obsidian keymap is used to add the `scheduled` or `priority` dataview property to a task — Task Card `1`–`4` picks a P-level and its frozen date, Enter opens explicit Schedule, and classic search (`/` or type to filter) reaches the same properties — or when `bob capture` uses `$<N>`, we add a `SCHEDULE LOG` bullet that contains one sub-bullet for each scheduling. Log grammar, opt-in markers, and blank-reason `🤷 no reason given` are unchanged.

### Stats Dash {#stats-dash}

*Aliases: dash_stats.*

`~/bob/dash_stats.md` (Obsidian aliases Stats, Dashboard Stats), whose
single `bob-stats` fence renders `bob stats` JSON: tiles, the focus
chart, day pinning, and family panels. "Where the time went" groups by
[Root Parent](#root-parent) by default, with sub-projects one click away, or by
[Task Type](#task-type). Opened from the dashboard STATS chip, Open Stats, or
any [Day Strip](#day-strip) fact. Not `dash.md` or the `bob stats` terminal output.

### Stats Strip {#stats-strip}

*Aliases: period strip, week strip, quarter strip, year strip.*

The read-only Stats summary that heads a [Period Note](#period-note) or a daily note, or appears
wherever a `bob-stats-strip` fence embeds one, for exactly one period: a day, an ISO
week, a 13- or 14-week quarter, an ISO year, or all time.

Every member has the same tiers, all painted from bob's values:

- five facts (Worked, Reviewed, Done, Created, Review closed), totalled over the
  period and marked `so far` while it is open. Each numeric fact sits over a quiet
  `typical` line: the median of the same-kind periods just before it, marked ▲/▼/=
  only once the period has closed;
- on periods, a [Root Parent](#root-parent) chart (the top N, `N more`, and hatched unattributed
  time) and a [Task Type](#task-type) chart (configured types, hatched untyped time) on one
  child-period axis; a column opens its child's note;
- a period-only Both/Roots/Types switch with its own memory, independent of the
  [Day Strip](#day-strip) controls.

Because periods are whole ISO weeks, the parts always add up to the whole. Worked
counts closed on-clock [Pomodoro](#pomodoro)s; [Off-Clock Pomodoro](#off-clock-pomodoro) time stays a quiet
separate hint.

The [Day Strip](#day-strip) is the day member: it keeps its two lanes, has no parts row, and
mounts itself in `bob-plan`. Facts and lanes open the [Stats Dash](#stats-dash) with the period
pinned. bob owns every value, and the strip never writes the note.

Not the parts table (`bob-period-parts`), the [Stats Dash](#stats-dash), `bob stats` terminal
output, or the [Morning GTD Review Footer](#morning-gtd-review-footer).

### Successor Offer {#successor-offer}

# Successor Offer

*Requested · project*

aka offer, pull-in offer

A [Task Successor](#task-successor) that a gesture may link under its Pomodoro destination is a
successor offer. A managed Done gesture offers the tasks it recovered, grouped as
direct hand-offs, residents of a recovered project, or project-finished pull-ins,
and, when it closes the task behind a [Leaf Project](#leaf-project)'s last live Task Link
today, that project's ready tasks as keep-moving offers, which are never
dependents.
Promoting a task that is linked in today's Pomodoros offers the new project note's
open tasks in that link's place. A capture `@route:id@` offers the new project
note's open tasks, never its `^prj`. Offers are not linked until explicitly picked;
a pick links the task and raises it to Next. A pick of an existing task also stamps
it fresh, while a task the same capture creates is never stamped. See
[Unblocked Tasks Are Offered, Never Auto-Linked](../develop/decisions.md#unblocked-tasks-are-offered).
The Mac Pull-In card labels offers from capture-created projects as a new project and
starts with nothing marked.

Parking or completing a task also offers the tasks linked to it with a configured
successor label (`starts after`) in their own relation group, which says which relation
and event fired and that they are not dependents.

### Task Decay {#task-decay}

*Aliases: decay, decay ladder, decay card, step down.*

The consent-based ladder that moves a repeatedly kept task one rung down, one
explicit answer at a time. Rungs: WIP (`[/]`; machine lane `pending`, the
user-facing alias of In Progress) → Next (`[*]`) → Ready (`[ ]` with no
priority) → P1 → P2 → P3 → P4 (each a `[priority::]` level). Blocked is an
overlay, never a rung.

Each rung allows a configured number of due Alt+F keeps (Bryan: 2 on every
rung). The allowance is the rung's `freshness.decay.pending_keeps` /
`next_keeps` / `ready_keeps` key (Ready and every P-level share `ready_keeps`),
then `freshness.decay.keeps`, then 3; `false` on one rung (or `decay: false`
overall) counts and logs but never asks. The priority property's per-level
`decay.rolls` (Bryan: 2) is the separate Ctrl+Enter same-level roll allowance,
not a keep allowance. A rung's N+1th due keep writes nothing and opens the
decay card: Enter steps exactly one rung down (P4 rolls again at P4), Alt+F
stays and restarts the [Keep Streak](#keep-streak) count, E rewords, D drops. Enter never
drops, nothing moves without a keypress, and nothing decays on a timer. Every
counted keep, stay, step, and drop writes one rung-qualified [Rotten Log](#rotten-log)
entry (a blank reason always logs 🤷); steps also write their [Schedule Log](#schedule-log)
decay entry. See [Task Decay Is One Ladder](../develop/decisions.md#task-decay-is-one-ladder).

### Task Dependency Link {#task-dependency-link}

*Aliases: task dep link, dep link.*

A plain (never transcluded) [Task Link](#task-link) to a prerequisite of another Obsidian
task. A task's dep links all sit on its Depends-On line, its first direct child:
`⛓️ **DEPENDS ON:** [[#^a]] • [[note#^b]]`. That line is the source of truth: Bob
derives the task's `[dependsOn::]` field and each target's `[id::]` from it, and
the task stays Blocked `[?]` while any target is open.
Each open prerequisite carries a generated `🧱 **BLOCKS:**` line listing its open
dependents, which Bob maintains from Depends-On lines and never reads back.
Dependencies are always stored on the dependent's line, but can be edited from
either end: Ctrl+Shift+B (Depends on) on the dependent or Ctrl+Shift+Alt+B
(Blocks…) on the prerequisite. A [Project Task](#project-task)'s dep
links sit on its own Depends-On line like any task's; while they are open, or
its inline `scheduled` is future, every open task in its note is Blocked. A
Blocked task keeps no Task Links under today's open Pomodoros: linking one
raises its open prerequisites instead, and `bob task reconcile` removes such
links. Add or remove dep links with Ctrl+Shift+P → Depends on, which
fuzzy-searches open tasks across the vault, or by editing the line. A dep link
is a prerequisite, not a sub-task: closing the dependent never closes its
targets, and dep links never count as Pomodoro Task Links. See
[Task Dependencies Are Links On One Depends-On Line](../develop/decisions.md#task-deps-are-depends-on-links) and
[Projects Block Their Tasks From The ^prj Line](../develop/decisions.md#projects-block-from-prj-line); syntax details live in
`docs/task-dependencies.md`.

### Task Drawer {#task-drawer}

*Aliases: drawer.*

A direct non-checkbox ALL-CAPS child bullet of a `#task` line, with its notes nested
beneath it. A drawer holds part of one task's work (`REQUIREMENTS`, `FUTURE WORK`);
its entries are plain bullets with no checkbox, `#task`, or `created` field. A drawer
is nonempty by construction: capture never creates an empty drawer, and promotion of a
task to a project note turns each drawer into an H2 section while reversal restores
them.

In capture, a `#` glued after `@route+id` always names a drawer (`@foo+bar#requirements`),
matched exactly against the target task at commit time and created on demand with the
catalog's most-used spelling. A quoted literal (`#"FUTURE WORK"`) or `--drawer TITLE`
forces creation and skips the near-duplicate guard; an unquoted slug that is a strict
prefix of, or edit distance 1 from, an existing drawer is refused. On a project's
`^prj` task, the note's eligible `##` sections are its drawers. `capture-complete`
lists the target's drawers in document order, then catalog recents, then a creation row,
with reserved, ambiguous, and near-duplicate choices refused and quorum copy authored by
bob. `bob capture-drawers` lists one task's drawers plus catalog recents.

In a capture draft, a `#` right after a first-level bullet's `- ` completes to the
drawer's title (`- #future-work` becomes `- FUTURE WORK`), and an ALL-CAPS first-level
bullet with nested notes is a drawer bullet, merging into an existing drawer under a
note-less `@route+id`. On a direct notebook-body route, `- #Section` instead selects
a notebook section for its nested notes; it is not a drawer. See
[Capture Bullets Mirror The Task Block](../develop/decisions.md#capture-bullets-mirror-the-task-block).

Managed lines and logs are never drawers: Depends-On, BLOCKS, [Task Relation](#task-relation) LINKS
lines, and the Schedule, Work, Rotten, and Cancel logs, plus `TASKS`. A drawer is not a
Markdown `##` heading, a [Project Note](#project-note) H2 section, an [Annotation Section](#annotation-section), a
[Pomodoro](#pomodoro) name, or a [Task Type](#task-type): `@note#Heading` routes to a note heading,
`=name` names a Pomodoro, and a free-standing `#fix` at an item edge, other than a
first-level bullet start, types the task.
See `docs/capture.md`.

### Task Freshness {#task-freshness}

*Aliases: freshness.*

The local calendar date a human last confirmed that an open task still needs doing as written, stored as `[fresh:: YYYY-MM-DD]` before the task's trailing Tasks fields. Supported Bob keymaps, Alt+F, and `bob capture` edits of existing tasks stamp it; creation and automation never do. A visible, non-recurring Ready task is due for review when it is new (no stamp), a tickler (its `scheduled` date arrived after the stamp, or it was automatically unblocked (`[unblocked::]`); machine state `resurfaced`), or rotten (the stamp is at least its interval old; machine `ROTTEN` since schema 2). The interval comes from `[refresh:: N]`, then the note's `task_refresh`, then `freshness.interval` (7 days) — except a Pending (WIP) or Next task in a walked lane, whose lane interval (`pending_interval` / `next_interval`, default 1 day; `false` walks that lane off) overrides the whole chain. The `]s` walk visits one shared queue in tiers PRE → NEW → PROJECTS → PENDING → NEXT → RECURRING → TICKLER → ROTTEN → POST; only due tasks walk (a task stamped today drops out). PRE/POST `#gtd` checklist rows (often recurring) resolve by completion, never by a stamp. A non-checklist recurring task is never stamped; once its occurrence date (earliest of scheduled, due, start) arrives it walks in RECURRING until completed, rescheduled past today, linked to Today, or cancelled. NEW holds unconfirmed tasks on `dash`, READY holds only confirmed/exempt tasks, and `rotten.md` holds TICKLER plus expired ROTTEN; see [Recurring Occurrences Walk When Due](../develop/decisions.md#recurring-occurrences-walk-when-due), [Review Walk Is Tiered With Daily Lane Review](../develop/decisions.md#review-walk-is-tiered), [READY Is Freshness-Gated With NEW and ROTTEN Review](../develop/decisions.md#ready-is-freshness-gated), [Today Is Read From The Ledger, Never Written To Tasks](../develop/decisions.md#today-is-read-from-the-ledger), and [Unblocked Tasks Resurface As Ticklers](../develop/decisions.md#unblocked-tasks-resurface-as-ticklers). Freshness never changes a lane, Today, schedule, or priority. Its status-bar view is the `s` walker footer — the [Morning GTD Review Footer](#morning-gtd-review-footer) shown while `s` is the active bracket walk. It is not Zorg `@FRESHNESS`, `bob vault-sync` freshness, or P-level scheduling windows. Freshness stamps alone never change a rung; only explicit decay-card answers do — see [Task Decay](#task-decay) and [Keep Streak](#keep-streak).

### Task Link {#task-link}

*Aliases: task block link.*

A block link to an Obsidian task. These can be located anywhere but, when they are the only contents of a sub-bullet on a pomodoro, they are treated as logged/planned tasks for that pomodoro. Task Links on a task's Depends-On line are [Task Dependency Link](#task-dependency-link)s. LINKS entries are [Task Relation](#task-relation)s, and generated LINKED FROM entries may be relations or inert [Task Mention](#task-mention)s; neither is ever a Pomodoro Task Link.

### Task Mention {#task-mention}

*Aliases: mention, text mention.*

An inert, derived back-reference from one task's own text to another, enabled by default. When
task S's title, a note under it, or a Cancel / Schedule / Work / Rotten Log
entry contains a block [Task Link](#task-link) to task T (`[[note#^id]]`, including
embeds and struck links), Bob stores `[[S]] (💬 mentions)` on T's generated
🪢 **LINKED FROM:** line. A mention is not a [Task Relation](#task-relation): it has no
label and no gestures, it is never a closing label, and it never enters the
label catalog. Nothing is written on S except a silent `^id`. A dependency
or an authored relation on the pair wins. See `docs/task-relations.md` §19.

### Task Merge {#task-merge}

# Task Merge

aka merge, merged into

Task Merge folds one or more source tasks into a target task, one of its drawers, or a
note section through `bob task merge`, capture's `>` or `<`, or the configured
`merged into` relation. It copies the source's notes to the destination and retires
each source as a cancelled tombstone that keeps them.
Dependent tasks and affected links are repaired, and the source records the target in
its `🪢 LINKS: merged into` line. See `docs/task-merge.md` for the contract and edge
cases. This task-outline operation is distinct from a [Merged Pomodoro](#merged-pomodoro), which
combines work sessions.

### Task Relation {#task-relation}

*Aliases: relation, LINKS line, LINKED FROM line.*

*Requested · project*

A directed, optionally labelled link from one task to another, inert unless its label
carries an effect. It is authored on
the source task's 🪢 **LINKS:** line and mirrored on the target task's generated 🪢
**LINKED FROM:** line. The generated LINKED FROM line also lists enabled-by-default [Task Mention](#task-mention)s
(`(💬 mentions)` entries), which are not relations. Add one with Capture `~` / `~~` or the Task Card `l` / `⇧L`
gestures. A relation is distinct from a Pomodoro [Task Link](#task-link): it never blocks a task,
counts as a Pomodoro Task Link, or changes its schedule, priority, or freshness.
Committing a configured cancel, complete, or merge label through capture or the Links
stage cancels the source, completes it, or merges it into the target by copying its notes
and cancelling it, respectively, at commit time; see [Task Merge](#task-merge).

A relation whose label is a configured successor label (such as `starts after`) also
offers its source as a [Successor Offer](#successor-offer) when its target is parked (left Pending with
no live Task Link today) or done; it still never blocks, and its mirror reads
`starts before`.

### Task Split {#task-split}

# Task Split

aka split, split out

Task Split promotes a splittable note under a task or eligible note section into a new
task. A task's selected bullet becomes a live task-link stub, and each new task gets a
generated mention back-link; a section bullet has no owning task to mention. Split does
not write a `split from` relation. Use `bob task split` or Ctrl+Shift+T. On a task line,
Ctrl+Shift+T opens a Tab-mark picker; on a drawer title, it scopes the picker to that
drawer. A daily-note task sends new tasks to its root note's `## Tasks` intake, or the
default inbox when it has no root; cross-note writes have a guarded Undo notice. See
`docs/task-split.md` for the contract and exact edits. This creates task identities,
distinct from splitting one [Pomodoro](#pomodoro) session's time record.

### Task Successor {#task-successor}

*Aliases: successor.*

# Task Successor

*Requested · project*

aka successor

A task positioned to take its predecessor's place in today's Pomodoro plan when the
predecessor leaves it. The successors of a managed Done gesture are the tasks it
unblocks: direct dependents, open residents of a project whose `^prj` it recovered,
and project-finished pull-ins, plus, when it closes the task behind a
[Leaf Project](#leaf-project)'s last live Task Link today, that project's ready tasks, which
need not depend on it. Promoting a task to a [Project Note](#project-note) makes the new
note's open tasks its successors, because the [Project Task](#project-task) never inherits the
predecessor's [Task Link](#task-link). Creating a project note with capture's `@route:id@`
likewise makes the new note's open tasks successors of its `^prj` task, the same way
promotion does. Successors are computed when the gesture runs and are never stored.
None is linked automatically: each becomes a [Successor Offer](#successor-offer), and only a picked
one is linked under its Pomodoro destination and raised to Next. Only a picked
existing task is stamped fresh, never a task the capture itself creates.

A predecessor also leaves the plan when a gesture parks it (Pending, no live Task Link
left today); parking or completing it offers every task linked to it with a successor
label such as `starts after`, which need not depend on it.
In Bob Mac Capture, project creation opens the Pull-In card with a New project context
and no offers marked.

### Task Type {#task-type}

*Aliases: type, theme, pomodoro theme, pomodoro-theme.*

A task's type is its kind of work: one ALL-CAPS name. Bob computes an open task's
effective type in this order: its explicit `[type:: NAME]` (or legacy `[theme:: NAME]`)
field; `plan.reading_type` for a reading task; the nearest area/project `task_type:`
default (or legacy `theme:`); then `plan.default_type`. A task field stores only an
exception to inheritance: choosing the inherited type clears it. Closed tasks keep
their fields as history.

A Pomodoro name can contain several `+`-separated components. With a configured
vocabulary, matching components are types and the others are labels; without one, each
component is a type unless it is an inventory label. A task's effective type and its
live Pomodoro Task Link agree: retyping updates the task field and moves or renames its
link as needed, while naming a linked entry retypes its open linked tasks. Writers
keep open names in agreement and `bob task reconcile` repairs today's open names,
never task fields ([Open Pomodoro Names Follow Task Links](../develop/decisions.md#open-pomodoro-names-follow-task-links)). PLAN is an
ordinary type, while `plan.exempt` only controls budget counting and mute color.

`bob types` manages the catalog and preferences; `bob themes` remains a CLI alias.
Configured `types:` colors take precedence, followed by journal pins, exempt and
unconfigured mute colors, the top-level area's color, and a stable name hash. Hiding a
type removes it from Recent suggestions only. See `docs/task-types.md`.

This is not a SASE bead `task_type`, a note's frontmatter `type:`, a Pomodoro home, or
an Obsidian appearance theme.

### Top-Level Project {#top-level-project}

*Aliases: top project.*

A [Project Note](#project-note) whose `parent` walk reaches an [Area Note](#area-note) before any
other project — normally its `parent` is an area, and a sub-area counts. A
project under another project is a sub-project at any depth and reports
under the top-level project above it, unless it — or a project between
them — sets `root: true`. It is the project grain of
[Root Parent](#root-parent) reporting: working time groups by root parent, never by
leaf project. "Top" is never folder depth, size, or status; see
`docs/pomodoro-homes.md`.

### Walker Footer {#walker-footer}

*Aliases: walk footer, lane footer, links footer.*

One contextual bob-ledger-tools status-bar panel that explains the active bracket walk. Exactly one member shows at a time, chosen by the persisted bracket family (`s` / `w` / `n`) — never by cursor, timer, or remaining work. The three members are the [Morning GTD Review Footer](#morning-gtd-review-footer) for `s`, the lane footer for `w` (a pure view over walk-membership counts with lane answer hints), and the links footer for `n` (a destination compass over the note's prev/next links). Every panel fills the same slots — glyph + position, current group, detail, hint, remaining groups, meter — wears its walk's hues, and sheds end-first as the bar narrows. A selected walk always paints, including calm clear states; clear is distinct from loading/unavailable (Tasks indexing, Today loading) and from the unset family, where no saved walk shows no panel. Positions are queue membership, never completion progress, and the panel is a read-only projection: it never stamps, moves, or creates tasks. While review commitments are due off-`s`, a quiet tier-tinted dot on the selector's `s` letter marks them. The walker footer is not the `[[ s w n ]]` selector, a landing toast, the [Day Strip](#day-strip), or a stats strip.

### Work Log {#work-log}

A task-local history of work performed, stored as a `🛠️ **WORK LOG**` direct child with newest-first summary sub-bullets. When `<ctrl+shift+enter>` unlinks an In Progress (`[/]`) task, its nonblank work summary is prepended; a blank summary leaves the log untouched, and the task stays In Progress. Alt+N releasing an In Progress task prompts for the same optional summary.
